status: ADDENDUM -- re-centres the READING of the running ladder on the question the user asked.  It edits nothing: PREREGISTRATION_PROTOTYPE_LADDER.json (sha 533adfbd...), its QMAX-referenced rule and _l1c_proto_summary.py stand as pre-registered and are reported as such (they answer 'can a few representatives replace stage 2 inside the composite').
user_clarification (verbatim, 2026-09-25: the point of this wasnt to make qmax better it was to see if we can instead of node voting do an ivfesque approach for selecting the parititions
what_was_misframed: the original pre-registration took QMAX (the stage-2 block max) as the reference at every level and put the headline at PRIMARY, where the dense and SPLADE node votes are still inside the fusion.  The question asked is whether an IVF-style coarse quantizer over the partitions can SELECT the partitions instead of node voting.
question: Can an IVF-style coarse quantizer over the served graph partitions -- q scored against a few fixed, query-free representatives per block, the top 50 blocks probed (nprobe = 50 = the P50 block budget), every node inside them served -- replace node voting (dense and SPLADE top-100 hits voting for their own block and the blocks of their directed STRUCT out-neighbours, rr(sum) + rr(max) per channel, frozen RRF = L1) without losing ALL-gold recall?
ivf_endpoint: the ladder's ALONE level: blocks ranked by the representative channel alone, top 50 probed, every node of a probed block served; ALL-gold = every gold node of the query inside a probed block.  Arms: CENT_MEAN, CENT_NORM (one centroid per block), FPS_m (m = 1 medoid .. 32 farthest-point prototypes, max over them), RAND_m (control), and the ladder's limit QMAX_ALONE (every node a representative; the limit of the ladder, not a coverage bound for smaller m).

references.primary: L1 = node voting (dense + SPLADE), the served routing
references.fair_dense_only: DENSE_VOTE_ALONE = the dense node vote alone (same out-neighbour memberships, no SPLADE)

rule.PRESERVES_NODE_VOTE(v, cache): exact McNemar of v_ALONE vs L1 on split A (already inside the record as arms[v_ALONE].ALL_vs_L1): net loss (lost - gained) <= TOL = max(2, round(0.005 * n_A)) (= 5 on every cache) AND NOT (lost > gained with p < 0.05)
rule.HEADLINE (text caches squad, squad_phg,: m*_text = the smallest ladder m at which FPS_m PRESERVES node voting on all three text caches: IVF_REPLACES_NODE_VOTING_ON_TEXT_AT_m=<m*> or IVF_DOES_NOT_REPLACE_NODE_VOTING_ON_TEXT
rule.universal (all five): already determined by the two metaqa caches, read before this addendum (below); reported as observed, not as a test
rule.also_reported: the same rule vs DENSE_VOTE_ALONE (dense-only fairness); RAND_m control; monotonicity in m; the recall ladder centroid -> prototypes -> ladder limit -> dense vote -> node vote per cache

honest_scope.three_differences_at_once: vs L1 the IVF arms differ in three ways: block-level instead of node-level scoring, no SPLADE side, and no out-neighbour votes (a node-vote hit also votes for its STRUCT out-neighbours' blocks; an IVF block sees only its own vectors).  DENSE_VOTE_ALONE removes the SPLADE difference only.

membership-expanded prototypes (a block represented over its nodes plus the nodes whose STRUCT out-edges point into it -- the IVF analogue of the out-neighbour vote)

honest_scope.compute: IVF: sum_B min(m, |B|) prototype products per query plus the in-block search of the 50 probed blocks (~5,000 nodes); node voting: a dense top-100 over all N nodes plus a SPLADE top-100 (the saving is real only against an exhaustive or ANN dense top-100)
